doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Classical piano lessons, quitting, and hearing jazz on the radio
summary: Started classical piano at seven, quit at about 15 against his parents' wishes, then fell for jazz heard late at night and bought books.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: You grew up at a time where there was no such thing as going to school to learn jazz.
How did you learn how to play it?

Well actually by, I don’t know, I guess we just bumped into each other because I officially started playing piano at seven years old, I started studying classical music. My people are from the West Indies and their hopes were for me to probably become a concert pianist you know, at the time that was not easily reached you know. But I kept going, and I started when I was about seven, and I studied until I was in my teens. I think I was about 15. And I just, all of a sudden I got kind of tired of playing, you might say, of the music. And I just stopped. And there was a lot of friction going on between me and my mother and my father you know. They were not too pleased with me at the time. But

after a while they just relented into the thing you know. I stopped playing for about a whole year. And within that time I started hearing, late at night, jazz wasn’t what you might say a thing that was on the radio or, it was recorded and everything, but it was more or less sort of a background thing. And let’s see, I started hearing it, little bits of it at night like around maybe 9, 8:30, 9, 10 o’clock in that area like, for maybe sometimes 15 minutes or half an hour you know. And I, you know, hadn’t played it or hadn’t been connected with it, it sounded good to me. The feeling. The what you might say, yeah, the feeling that it gave me. I said gee I like that. And I even went and bought some books and sort of tried to, you might say, set myself up musically with the music you know. Meaning that, I figured that way, if I did that then just playing after a while would come naturally, which it did.
